newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean companies donate fertilizers to N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean companies donate fertilizers to N.Korea.

text.p: Nine South Korean chemical companies on Wednesday pledged to donate 800 tonnes of fertilizers to help ease a chronic food shortage in impoverished North Korea, an industry group said.

The Korea Fertilizer Industry Association said its nine members planned to hand over the fertilizers to the Red Cross, the only authorised channel for South Korea's private-level aid to the North, this month.
The donations by the nine, including Namhae Chemical Co, Dongbu Hannong Chemical Co and Chinhae Chemical Co, were worth 200 million won ($224,000), an association statement said.
"We hope the North Korean farmers will not lose hope and courage," the statement quoted Namhae Chemical President Lee Dong-hoon as saying. The company promised to donate 334 tonnes.
"We hope the step of conveying the sympathy and consolation of South Korea's fertilizer producers will serve as a stepping stone for better South-North relations," he said.
North Korea, which was hit hard by devastating floods in 1995 and 1996, said earlier this month an unprecedented drought and heatwave damaged much of this year's crops.
North Korea watchers in Seoul say natural disasters only worsened a chronic food shortage in the North. The shortages have amounted to between one and two million tonnes a year since the 1980s.

The Korean Sharing Movement, a South Korean civic group which has been actively campaigning to aid the North, has already delivered 2,000 tonnes of fertilizers to Pyongyang through the South Korean Red Cross.
The group said fertilizers were essential to increase the North's agricultural output.

The South Korean Red Cross, which has promised $20 million worth of food supplies to the North, said it would contact its North Korean counterpart once it received the fertilizers and the Seoul government approved the aid.
